text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate from dedicated pool `dp-chi-42` serving tenant `T-981` (AcmeCorp) in `vpc-acme-eu-prod`. Start: 2026-03-15T04:07Z. Paging @jamie_oncall. Link: https://metrics.redwood.local/alerts/1779000000

jamie_oncall: saw it, acked. oncall taking. Starting triage now.

priya_sre: quick check — CPU fine, but node OOMs reported on 3 instances in the pool. Error traces show `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` in model worker, repeated KV cache eviction logs.

alejandro_eng: adding context: this pool is a dedicated GPU pool pinned to AcmeCorp. Model is `acme/large-v3.2.1-quant`. Recent deploy? No, last deploy 3 days ago.

maria_cs: tagging for customer comms — I'm on standby. Acme's SREs are already filing a ticket with their network team (they have private peering). Will escalate to account exec after initial impact summary.

jamie_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) drain `dp-chi-42` from routing for Acme only, 2) fail requests to their warm-fallback pool `dp-chi-43`, 3) rolling restart workers on the 3 affected nodes, 4) if needed, bump pool count + add GPUs. Doing step 1 now.

incident-bot: Routing change applied: `dp-chi-42` marked `out_of_rotation` for tenant `T-981` at 04:12Z.

priya_sre: logs from one worker: ```
[2026-03-15T04:05:31Z] ERROR worker-12 oom: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate 512MB
[2026-03-15T04:05:31Z] WARN kvcache: eviction threshold reached, evicted 1200 entries
[2026-03-15T04:05:32Z] WARN routing: retrying request to fallback pool
```

alejandro_eng: hypothesis: quantized kernel in v3.2.1 has a memory fragmentation bug under long seq > 2048 with prefix caching churn. Repro attempt on canary starting.

evan_eng: starting canary on `dp-chi-43` with same model but with limited KV cache size to test. Command: `infractl pool scale --pool dp-chi-43 --replicas 4 && infractl annotate pool dp-chi-43 kvcache.max=256MB`

maria_cs: customer impact (preliminary): ~30% of Acme inference calls returned 5xx/timeout during spike window. Estimated affected requests ~6k in last 20m. Their SLAs (Dedicated) are 99.9% uptime per month — we'll need to calculate prorated credit if confirmed. I will not promise credits yet.

ops_lead: good containment so far. Any cross-tenant impact?

priya_sre: confirmed — isolation held. No errors observed in other customers hosted on shared pools. Only `dp-chi-42` (dedicated to T-981) affected. However, the router retries to fallback pool increased tail latency for a small fraction of shared-hosted traffic for ~2m.

jamie_oncall: rolling restart triggered on affected nodes (04:18Z). Observed worker processes restarting one by one.

incident-bot: Metric update: 5xx rate for `dp-chi-42` dropped from 24% -> 1.8% across 5m after restart and drain. Latency P95 normalized.

jamie_oncall: mitigation successful. Keeping pool drained while we investigate root cause. Will start memory heap dumps and collect trace artifacts.

alejandro_eng: collected heapdump and kernel logs. Early analysis supports memory fragmentation + cache eviction pattern. Need kernel patch or fallback to non-quantized kernel for that model. Running a repro with synthetic long-seq load (seq len 4096) -> failure reproduced in ~7 minutes.

evan_eng: short-term mitigation we can ship quickly: fallback the model runtime to `float16` kernel (non-quantized) for affected pool image to avoid fragmentation while patch is developed. That will increase token cost by ~20% but should be stable.

maria_cs: customer update draft (for ACME CTO): "We experienced elevated error rates affecting AcmeCorp's dedicated inference pool in EU region for ~20m. We've fully contained the issue to your dedicated pool, failed over traffic to a healthy warm-fallback, and applied restarts. We're performing a deep root-cause analysis and will provide an RCA and timeline within 48 hours. We'll also coordinate on any SLA credits as appropriate." Thoughts?

account_exec: send that ASAP to the CTO. Please CC me and legal. Keep language measured, avoid commitments on credits until ops_fin confirms.

ops_lead: action items so far: - AC-1 (jamie_oncall): keep pool drained, coordinate heapdump upload — due 2026-03-15 06:00Z - AC-2 (alejandro_eng): full repro & kernel patch PR if confirmed — due 2026-03-17 - AC-3 (evan_eng): produce temporary runtime fallback plan and rollout to `dp-chi-42` image set — due 2026-03-15 10:00Z - AC-4 (maria_cs): send customer update and prepare exec update — due 2026-03-15 05:00Z - AC-5 (ops_lead): estimate SLA credit exposure, loop in finance — due 2026-03-16

priya_sre: adding monitoring rule improvement: alert when dedicated pool OOMs > 1 in 5m and KV eviction rate > 500/s. Will submit patch to alerts repo.

jamie_oncall: posting final incident state update for this thread: mitigation applied, pool drained, fallback in place, no cross-tenant impact, collecting artifacts. Leaving a note for followup RCA. Handing off to night team in 2h.

maria_cs: customer emailed with the drafted note and logged a high-priority support ticket. Acme requested an exec-level summary and proposed credits; asked for timeline for RCA and fix.

alejandro_eng: root cause summary (draft): "A memory fragmentation regression in the quantized GPU kernel for model v3.2.1 under long-sequence workloads caused OOMs in dedicated worker processes when combined with aggressive KV cache eviction. This was triggered under Acme's workload patterns and resulted in worker restarts and elevated 5xx rates for the dedicated pool."

evan_eng: suggested remediation list: 1) backport kernel fix + release v3.2.2, 2) add runtime guard to fallback to float16 kernel if kvcache.evictions spike, 3) enforce per-tenant KV cache quotas to avoid unbounded usage in dedicated pools, 4) add synthetic long-seq canary tests in staging with quantized kernel.

ops_lead: exec update draft to internal execs: "Acme dedicated pool experienced a 20-minute availability degradation due to a quantized kernel memory fragmentation issue. Contained to dedicated pool, mitigations applied, long-term fix in progress. Potential SLA exposure under evaluation. RCA to be delivered in 48 hours."

maria_cs: customers asked for credits suggestion. I propose we estimate prorated downtime and propose 25% of daily committed capacity for the minute-window affected and offer 5k platform credits as goodwill while investigation continues. Finance to confirm.

account_exec: do not promise the 5k yet. Ok to offer investigation support and expedited fix timeline. Finance/ops to confirm credit numbers before external commit.

priya_sre: tagging next steps in runbook: update dedicated-pool runbook with eviction thresholds, add explicit drain-check before routing pool back into prod, create automated canary for quantized kernel on long seq.

jamie_oncall: handoff note: if the night oncall sees repeat OOMs on `dp-chi-42` (or `dp-chi-43` after fallback) — contact alejandro_eng and evan_eng immediately, keep pool drained, and open an incident call.

incident-bot: Thread status: mitigated -> postmortem_pending. Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-ACME-01.

maria_cs: taking ownership of exec-facing comms and will circulate polished RCA draft to this channel and to account_exec + legal. Expect initial RCA draft in ~24h.

alejandro_eng: attaching artifact links (heapdump, kernel-logs, repro script): https://artifacts.redwood.local/incidents/INC-2026-0315-ACME-01

ops_lead: closing note: good cross-team coordination. Extra credit to oncall for fast containment. We'll reconvene for RCA review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
